knowledgePattern: Use paired products to simplify reciprocals of a geometric progression

hints.title: Write the GP terms and compare products
hints.body: Express the four terms using their first term and positive ratio. Compare the products of the two outer terms and the two inner terms.
hints.recap: GP positions correspond to successive powers of a common ratio.
hints.pitfall: The pair sums do not themselves form a GP.
hints.pause: Use the product relation to simplify the paired reciprocals.

recall.reminder: GP positions correspond to successive powers of a common ratio.

hints.title: Eliminate the first term
hints.body: Divide the two given pair-sum equations, then factor the numerator and denominator in the ratio.
hints.recap: Factoring can expose common nonzero factors before cancellation.
hints.pitfall: Check positivity before dividing by the common ratio or a sum involving it.
hints.pause: Find a relation involving the ratio and its reciprocal.

recall.reminder: Factoring can expose common nonzero factors before cancellation.

hints.title: Recover the shared product
hints.body: Expand the square of the inner pair sum and divide by the inner product. Relate that result to the ratio expression you found.
hints.recap: A common denominator combines fractions while preserving their full numerators.
hints.pitfall: Keep both cross terms when squaring a sum.
hints.pause: Calculate the product and then the required sum of reciprocals.

recall.reminder: A common denominator combines fractions while preserving their full numerators.

solution:
1. Write the terms as a,ar,ar2,ar3, where r>0. The products ad and bc are equal; call their common value P. Pairing reciprocals gives 1/a+1/d=(a+d)/P and 1/b+1/c=(b+c)/P, so the target is 65/P.

2. The ratio of the supplied sums is 3530=1+r3r+r2=r2−r+1r=r+1/r−1. Hence r+1/r=13/6. Cancellation is valid because r>0.

3. Now (b+c)2/(bc)=r+2+1/r=25/6, giving P=900/(25/6)=216. Therefore the reciprocal sum is 65/216. Answer A.

4. As a check, the ratios are 3/2 or 2/3, producing terms 8,12,18,27 or their reverse; each has the required pair sums and products.
